read RDS files
```{r}
SRR30016494<-readRDS("<original_archive>/scRNA_PRJNA1141235/RDS_files/SRR30016494.RDS")
SRR30016499<-readRDS("<original_archive>/scRNA_PRJNA1141235/RDS_files/SRR30016499.RDS")
SRR30016501<-readRDS("<original_archive>/scRNA_PRJNA1141235/RDS_files/SRR30016501.RDS")
SRR30016504<-readRDS("<original_archive>/scRNA_PRJNA1141235/RDS_files/SRR30016504.RDS")
```

merge objects into 1
```{r}
merged<-merge(x=SRR30016494, y=c(SRR30016499, SRR30016501, SRR30016504),
              add.cell.ids=c("94","99","01","04"),
              project='merged')
#ls: tells you how many objects and the order
```

PREPROCESSING WORKFLOW
step 1: quality control:
```{r}
#store mito % in object meta data
merged<-PercentageFeatureSet(merged,pattern = "^MT-", col.name = "percent_mt")

#select cells for further analysis
subset_merged<-subset(merged, subset = nFeature_RNA > 500 & nCount_RNA < 20000 & percent_mt < 25)
#& nFeature_RNA < 8000
```
Plot to see distribution of cells
```{r}
VlnPlot(merged, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent_mt"), ncol = 3)
VlnPlot(subset_merged, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent_mt"), ncol = 3)

```
AFTER QC: cell count goes from ~32,000 to ~10,000
step 2: data normalization:
```{r}
#normalize
subset_merged<-NormalizeData(subset_merged, normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)
#normalizes gene expression measurement for each cell by the total expression then multiples by a scale factor of 10,000
```

step 3: identification of highly variable features 

```{r}
#find variable features
subset_merged<-FindVariableFeatures(subset_merged, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)
VariableFeaturePlot(subset_merged)

#Fu 2024: "2000 highly variable genes were selected"
```
step 4: data scaling
```{r}
subset_merged<-ScaleData(subset_merged)
#highly expressed genes will not dominate downstream analysis

#save
#saveRDS(subset_merged, file = "<original_archive>/scRNA_PRJNA1141235/merged_RDS_may21")
```

PCA
```{r}
subset_merged<-RunPCA(subset_merged)
```
plot
```{r}
DimPlot(subset_merged, reduction = "pca", dims = c(1,2))
DimPlot(subset_merged, reduction = "pca", dims = c(1,10))
DimPlot(subset_merged, reduction = "pca", dims = c(1,50))
```
determine the 'dimension' of the dataset
- decide how many of those summary axes (PCs) are meaningful before you start clustering
- An elbow plot shows how much each PC contributes; you look for the point where the contribution “bends” (the elbow)
```{r}
#JackStraw function is more complex and challenging to understand
#ElbowPlot function
ElbowPlot(subset_merged)
#identify where the elbow is --> around 9
ElbowPlot(subset_merged, ndims = 50, reduction = "pca")
#just to check
```

cluster the cells
```{r}
subset_merged<-FindNeighbors(subset_merged, dims = 1:20)
#takes first 20 PCA and finds dimensional analysis, and finds cells with similar feature expression pattern
#builds a network map where each cell connects to its nearest neighbors based on the first 20 PCs

#subset_merged<-FindClusters(subset_merged, resolution = 0.1)
#resolution=0.1--> 12 clusters

subset_merged<-FindClusters(subset_merged, resolution = 0.8)
#resolution=0.3--> 17 clusters

```
run non-linear dimensional analysis:
UMAP:
```{r}
subset_merged<-RunUMAP(subset_merged, dims = 1:20)
DimPlot(subset_merged, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)
```
tSNE:
```{r}
subset_merged<-RunTSNE(object=subset_merged)
DimPlot(object= subset_merged, reduction = "tsne")
```
- highlighting local groupings
- distances between far-apart clusters can be less meaningful
